outline.chapter_title: Overview of Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
outline.description: Introduces why mathematical reasoning is pivotal for AI systems, outlines key benchmark datasets such as GSM8K and MATH, explains the persistent performance gap between open-source models and proprietary giants like GPT‑4/Gemini Ultra, and motivates focused domain-specific modeling.
subtopics: Role mathematics plays in AI research

outline.description: Summarizes the primary goals driving DeepSeekMath—bridging the open‑source/performance divide while keeping models publicly accessible—highlighting contributions including large-scale math corpus construction, investigation into code pre‑training effects, introduction of Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), and insights showing smaller models can rival larger closed ones.
subtopics: Bridging performance gap while staying open-source

outline.description: Details the systematic pipeline for extracting mathematical text from Common Crawl using FastText classifiers trained on OpenWebMath seeds, deduplication strategies applied to billions of HTML pages, iterative enrichment loops incorporating manual annotation from identified domains such as mathoverflow.net, decontamination against existing benchmark texts using exact n‑gram matching, and analysis revealing strong multilingual coverage.
subtopics: Deduplication strategies applied to Common Crawl
Iterative enrichment loop via manual annotation

outline.description: Presents controlled experiments comparing models trained separately on different mathematical corpora—including MathPile, OpenWebMath, Proof-Pile—to demonstrate that the DeepSeekMath Corpus yields superior downstream accuracy across multiple benchmarks while achieving steeper learning curves even under limited token budgets.
subtopics: Learning curve analysis over token budgets

outline.description:
Describes initializing from DeepSeek-Coder base architecture followed by extensive continual training over 500B tokens comprising a diverse mix—56% math corpus tokens from DeepSeekMath Corpus, plus code tokens from Github/Amazon Web Services repositories—and evaluates its capabilities through chain-of-thought prompting without tools, program-of-thought prompting leveraging Python libraries like sympy/mathematics modules,
integration into formal theorem proving pipelines using miniF2F Isabelle/Sledgehammer,
and measuring general NLP/coding benchmark improvements such as MMLU/BBH/HumanEval/MBPP.
subtopics: Formal autoformalization via miniF2F Isabelle integration
